fix(agent): translate workspace directory access to recoverable tool error (#54)

`workspace_read_file` and the other workspace IO tools used to crash the
run with a non-retryable `agent.internal_error` when the model targeted
a directory (e.g. `persist`, `output`) instead of a regular file: the
underlying `fs::read_to_string` raised `EISDIR`, which the repository
surfaced as `DomainError::InternalError`.

We now model "the target is a directory" as a domain-level conflict and
let the tool layer translate it into a model-facing recoverable error:

- `DomainError::Conflict(String)` added at the domain layer; mapped to
  `ApplicationError::ValidationError`, `CommandError::BadRequest`, and
  HTTP 409 in the LAN sync server (all 3 exhaustive matches updated).
- `file_agent_repository::workspace_store::ensure_target_is_not_directory`
  probes `fs::symlink_metadata` in `read_text` / `write_text` and raises
  `DomainError::Conflict("workspace.path_is_directory: ...")` before
  hitting `EISDIR`.
- A shared `parse_workspace_conflict_message` lives in
  `agent_tools/common.rs` (re-exported `pub(crate)`) so both the
  workspace tool layer (`classify_workspace_io_error` in `args.rs`) and
  the runtime-service commit hook (`perform_host_chat_commit`) decode
  the conflict into a `workspace.path_is_directory` recoverable tool
  result through a single source of truth.
- `workspace_read_file` description tightened to explicitly forbid
  directory targets and point at `workspace_list_files` instead.

Tests:
- Repository-level: `read_text` / `write_text` on a directory return
  `DomainError::Conflict` with the documented prefix.
- Tool layer: `classify_workspace_io_error` maps Conflict ->
  `workspace.path_is_directory`, NotFound -> `workspace.file_not_found`,
  and bubbles unknown errors for the dispatcher to fail-fast on.

fix(agent): emit run_rollback_targets + userRetryable on instruction drift (#55)

When the model deviated from the tool contract after committing chat
artifacts (e.g. answered with plain text instead of calling
`workspace_finish`), the run failed with `model.tool_call_required` /
`agent.tool_after_finish` / `agent.max_tool_rounds_exceeded`, but the
already-committed messages were left orphaned in chat and the UI had no
signal to offer a Retry path.

Loop runner now tracks each `AgentToolEffect::ChatCommitted` during a
run. When the run later enters a drift state, it emits a
`run_rollback_targets` warn event BEFORE `run_failed`, listing the
`{ path, mode, messageId, round }` of every commit the host UI needs to
roll back.

`run_failed` payload gains a `userRetryable: bool` flag:
- `retryable=true` (transient / rate-limited) implies `userRetryable=true`.
- Otherwise drift codes (`model.tool_call_required`,
  `agent.tool_after_finish`, `agent.max_tool_rounds_exceeded`) are
  `userRetryable=true` while remaining auto-non-retryable, so the UI can
  surface a manual Retry button after performing the rollback. Policy /
  validation errors stay `userRetryable=false`.

`workspace_commit` description tightened to spell out the
"commit -> finish in the same or next turn, never plain text" contract.

Docs:
- `docs/Agent/RunEventJournal.md`: new `run_rollback_targets` event,
  expanded `run_failed` payload schema with `userRetryable` semantics.
- `docs/Agent/ToolSystem.md`: documents the

feat(diagnostics): log upstream body preview when chat completion JSON parse fails

When an upstream chat-completion provider returns 2xx with a body the client
cannot decode as JSON (HTML challenge pages, plain-text proxy errors, empty
bodies, SSE on a non-stream endpoint, etc.), the failure used to silently bubble
up as `Failed to parse generation JSON` with no log of what was actually
received, leaving operators without any signal to diagnose CDN/proxy issues.

Introduce a shared body-preview helper in
`infrastructure/apis/http_chat_completion_repository/body_preview.rs`:

* `log_upstream_body_parse_failure(provider, operation, status, content_type,
  body, error)` emits a structured `tracing::error!` event with a UTF-8 lossy
  preview of the first 512 bytes plus the full body length, so logs stay bounded
  even when upstream pours out megabytes of HTML.
* `read_upstream_json_body(provider, operation, response)` is the async wrapper
  every HTTP provider call site uses: it reads the body once, attempts JSON
  decode, calls the logger on failure, and surfaces a more diagnostic error
  string (`Failed to parse {operation} JSON from {provider} (status {n})`).

All twelve `response.json::<Value>().await.map_err(...)` call sites across the
seven provider modules (`openai`, `claude`, `cohere`, `makersuite`,
`gemini_interactions`, `vertexai`, `openai_responses`) now route through the
helper. The OpenAI Responses WebSocket message parser
(`parse_ws_event`) also calls the logger before returning so non-JSON frames
emit the same diagnostic.

Error classification is intentionally unchanged in this commit (still
`DomainError::InternalError`); the follow-up will reclassify it as transient.

fix(agent): reclassify upstream invalid response as transient retryable

Chat completion JSON-parse / body-read failures used to surface as
`DomainError::InternalError`, which `error_payload::is_retryable` treats as
non-retryable `agent.internal_error`. In practice these failures are caused by
upstream-side hiccups (CDN HTML challenges, proxy timeouts mid-body, plain-text
200 errors, SSE on a non-stream endpoint) and tearing down the run is the wrong
default — the user just sees an opaque permanent failure.

Reclassify the helper to return `DomainError::Transient` carrying the
`model.upstream_invalid_response` structured prefix so:

* `From<DomainError> for ApplicationError` maps it to `ApplicationError::Transient`,
* `error_payload::structured_code_and_message` extracts the
  `model.upstream_invalid_response` code so the frontend can present a coherent
  error,
* `error_payload::is_retryable` reports `retryable=true`.

The OpenAI Responses WebSocket message parser uses the same prefix and helper
so WS-frame JSON failures behave identically to HTTP-body JSON failures.

No new `DomainError` variant: this reuses the existing `Transient` variant, so
the three exhaustive `From<DomainError>` / `map_domain_error` match arms are
untouched.

Adds a regression test in `error_payload::tests` asserting that an
`ApplicationError::Transient` whose message starts with
`model.upstream_invalid_response:` produces `code=model.upstream_invalid_response`
and `retryable=true`.

fix(agent): preserve prior swipes when rolling back drift commits

PR review surfaced that the rollback path for `run_rollback_targets`
was always calling `deleteMessage(index)`, which wipes the entire chat
entry — including any swipes the user had authored before the agent
run started. For regenerate / swipe generation types the run only
appends a new swipe in-place via `saveReply({ type: 'swipe' })`, so
nuking the whole message is too aggressive.

Captures the rollback strategy at commit time on
`extra.tauritavern.agent.rollback`:

- If the first `saveReply` call grew `chat.length` (the run created a
  new chat entry), strategy is `deleteMessage`.
- Otherwise the run appended a swipe to a pre-existing assistant
  message, strategy is `deleteSwipe` with the new swipe's id.

The rollback helper now branches on that strategy: it calls vendor's
exported `deleteSwipe(swipeId, messageId)` for swipe-mode targets
(only when the swipes array still has more than one entry so vendor's
"can't delete the last swipe" toastr never fires), and falls back to
`deleteMessage` otherwise. Messages persisted before this field
existed default to the old `deleteMessage` behavior, so no migration
is needed.

No vendor file is touched: `deleteSwipe` is already exported from
`src/script.js`, the bridge change lives in
`src/tauri/main/api/agent-chat-commit-bridge.js`, and the rollback
helper is project-owned.

Tests: two new cases on the rollback helper — one drives the
deleteSwipe path against a 3-swipe message and asserts that the
prior swipes (`'user-authored'`, `'user-authored alt 1'`) survive
while the agent's appended swipe is popped; the other asserts the
fallback to `deleteMessage` when the swipe array is a singleton.

feat(agent): soft drift recovery + strengthen workspace.commit hint (#64)

Background
----------
Issue surfaced in production: model uses tools correctly through the
full pipeline (write_file → commit), then on the round expected to call
workspace_finish, replies with the full content as plain assistant text
instead. The committed message survives but the run fails with
`model.tool_call_required`, leaving an orphaned chat message and the UI
locked. PR #62 (issue #55) added rollback signalling so the host can
unwind cleanly, but the model's work is still discarded.

Two complementary fixes:

1. Strengthen `workspace.commit`'s tool result string with an explicit
   "REQUIRED NEXT STEP: call workspace_finish" reminder + a
   `nextRequiredTool` field in structured payload. This is the highest
   attention real-estate in the prompt (last tool result the model sees
   before the next turn) and costs essentially nothing.

2. Soft drift recovery: when the model returns 0 tool calls, give it
   ONE corrective nudge instead of failing immediately. We push the
   model's drifted text into history (so it owns what it said) and
   append a synthetic `user` reminder that distinguishes the post-commit
   case (commit will be rolled back) from the no-commit case (every
   turn must use a tool). If the model recovers (any tool call) the
   run continues normally; if it drifts again, we fall through to the
   existing #55 path (rollback + `userRetryable=true`).

   Hard cap of 1 attempt per run via `DRIFT_RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`
   prevents token-bombing on stubborn drifters. Multi-turn pattern
   verified against Anthropic + OpenAI docs as API-compatible (no
   role-alternation constraint after no-tool-use turn).

Backward compatibility
----------------------
- Failed recovery falls through to existing #55 code path: same
  `model.tool_call_required` error, same `run_rollback_targets` event,
  same `userRetryable=true`. No frontend changes required for the
  failure case.
- New `drift_recovery_attempted` event is additive; old hosts ignore.
- Existing #55 drift test extended to include the recovery attempt
  before falling through to rollback.

Tests
-----
- `foreground_run_emits_rollback_targets_on_tool_call_required_drift`:
  updated to assert exactly one `drift_recovery_attempted` precedes the
  rollback when the model drifts twice in a row.
- `foreground_run_recovers_from_post_commit_drift_with_nudge`: new —
  model drifts after commit, gets nudged, complies with finish; run
  completes, no rollback, commit preserved. Also asserts the nudge text
  reaches the model verbatim.
- `foreground_run_recovers_from_no_commit_drift_with_nudge`: new —
  model drifts on turn 1, gets nudged, completes the full pipeline.

601 lib tests passing.

Docs
----
- `RunEventJournal.md`: documents `drift_recovery_attempted` event +
  recovery flow.
- `ToolSystem.md`: spells out the soft-recovery contract and which
  drift codes do/don't get the second chance.

feat(chat): add Claude on AWS Bedrock as a dedicated chat completion source

Adds end-to-end support for invoking Claude models through the AWS Bedrock
Anthropic API as a first-class `claude_aws` chat completion source instead
of overloading the existing Claude vendor path.

Backend (src-tauri/):
- New `ChatCompletionSource::ClaudeAws` enum variant with parse/key/display
  mapping, plus `SecretKeys::CLAUDE_AWS` and `CLAUDE_AWS_REGION`.
- New payload builder `payload/claude_aws.rs` that normalizes Bedrock model
  IDs (e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`)
  back to the canonical Anthropic identifiers before delegating to the
  Claude builder so that thinking, sampling and contract resolution all
  pick the right capabilities for Claude 4.x.
- New HTTP repository `http_chat_completion_repository/claude_aws.rs`
  that:
  * targets `bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com`, sends the
    Anthropic Messages payload with `Authorization: Bearer …` and
    decodes the AWS EventStream binary streaming format back into SSE
    chunks for the existing stream pipeline;
  * implements dynamic `list_models` against the control plane
    (`bedrock.{region}.amazonaws.com/foundation-models` plus
    `/inference-profiles`), merging foundation models with
    cross-region inference profiles and filtering out foundation
    entries whose `inferenceTypesSupported` does not include
    `ON_DEMAND` (which would otherwise surface IDs that can only be
    invoked through an inference profile).
- DTO/config glue: `chat_completion_dto.rs` carries `claude_aws_region`,
  `config.rs` derives `bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com`, and the
  source participates in regular status validation (no `noValidate`
  bypass).
- Adapt the new upstream `llm_connection_service` to map `ClaudeAws`
  to its secret key so the exhaustive match keeps compiling.

Frontend (src/):
- Wires `claude_aws` through `chat_completion_sources`, `SECRET_KEYS`,
  the autoconnect probe in `RossAscends-mods.js` and the per-source
  `data-source` whitelists in `index.html` (system prompt, function
  calling, web search, media inlining, …).
- New API form with API key, region input and a `Bedrock Model ID`
  select that is populated dynamically from `list_models` with grouped
  `<optgroup>` sections (Foundation models / Cross-region inference
  profiles). The hardcoded fallback options purposefully list only
  Claude 4.x `us./global.` inference profiles and Claude 3.x ON_DEMAND
  foundation models to mirror the runtime filter above.
- Expose the global `Request model reasoning`, `Reasoning Effort`
  dropdown and the Claude-style thinking-budget hint to the
  `claude_aws` source. Without this, the globally-shared
  `oai_settings.reasoning_effort` could silently leak into Bedrock
  requests (the UI was hidden but the value still propagated), forcing
  adaptive thinking on every turn and producing the "first byte after
  ~13s + mid-stream stall" symptom observed during testing.

Tests:
- `tests/claude-aws-provider-contract.test.mjs` covers the Rust enum
  wiring, the secret key constant, the new form, the autoconnect probe
  and the reasoning UI whitelists.
- Unit tests for model-ID normalization (Opus 4.6 manual-or-adaptive,
  Opus 4.7 adaptive), control-plane URL derivation, the ON_DEMAND
  filter and the merged Anthropic model listing live next to the new
  modules.

fix(chat): tolerate JSON null for custom additional parameters

`/api/backends/chat-completions/generate` forwards the request body
verbatim, so any null that the frontend writes into
`custom_include_body` / `custom_exclude_body` / `custom_include_headers`
ends up in the Rust payload as `Value::Null`. The shared `optional_string`
helper currently rejects that with a `ValidationError`:

  "Chat completion request field must be a string: custom_include_headers"

surfacing to the user as `Failed to generate chat completion`.

In practice the field is *semantically absent* — a stale preset cleared the
slot, or a per-chat API-router extension persisted a sparse JSON object.
Treating `null` as "missing" matches serde's default `Option<String>`
behaviour at deserialization boundaries and keeps the HTTP edge forgiving
without weakening the type check for genuine misuse (numbers, arrays and
objects still fail fast).

Fix is one branch in `optional_string`; all three custom_* slots benefit
because they share that helper. New unit test pins the null-tolerance
contract.

part reuses the existing in-memory path; the out-of-window part flushes
pending saves first, then calls the new command and swaps the windowed
cursor only if the chat and cursor offset are still the ones the rewrite

fix(dev): stop fs.watch last-access noise from looping page reloads

On Windows hosts with NTFS last-access updates enabled (fsutil behavior
DisableLastAccess 0/2), every read of a file under src/ updates its
last-access time, and recursive fs.watch reports that as a change event.
The dev server then reloaded the page for any non-bundled path: fonts,
styles, images and other static assets fetched by the page itself.
Each reload fetched those assets again, producing a reload -> fetch ->
last-access -> reload feedback loop where any UI interaction kept
refreshing the page.

Two guards in handleFrontendChange:

- Directory-level change events arrive with a null filename and cannot
  identify a reloadable file; ignore them instead of reloading.
- A last-access update never changes mtime, so a change event whose
  mtime is far in the past is read noise, not an edit. Only reload for
  files written within the last 30 seconds. Trade-off: writers that
  deliberately preserve mtime no longer trigger a reload.

Verified on Windows (DisableLastAccess=2): two rounds of fetching 12
static assets produced zero reload events (previously 8 in one round),
while a real file write still triggered exactly one reload.

perf(regex): gate scripts on required literals #238

Creator regexes are dominated by tag pairs, and the pathological ones share
one shape: an unanchored prefix such as `[\s\S]*?</guide>` whose closing
literal is absent from the text. Both regress and V8 then restart at every
position and scan to the end each time, so a 60k-character message costs
seconds per script.

pattern-requirements.js derives, per top-level alternative, the literals
every match must contain (a conjunction of choices, so `</think>|</thinking>`
is one requirement). gated-replace.js uses them three ways: skip the script
when no alternative can match, prefix alternatives that cannot match with
`(?!)` so they fail in O(1) per position without touching capture numbering,
and stop a global search once no live alternative's literals remain ahead of
the cursor. Anything the analyser does not understand contributes nothing,
and only literals whose meaning is flag-independent are extracted, so
`\u{…}`, `\p{…}`, `\k<…>` and surrogate halves are opaque.

The worker announces a script only when its regex will actually run, which
also makes the timeout measure real work. This subsumes the tag-prefix
literal gate.

On the captured 16-script chain a 35,806-character message drops from 2.8 s
to 3 ms in V8; 312k real script × text pairs and 265k fuzzed cases are
byte-identical to String.prototype.replace.

perf(regex): share portable scripts across a batch

Each task carried its own copies of the portable script objects, so the

write re-serialized and re-transmitted the whole history. It now

blocking task; JS and IPC work is proportional to the header.

also invalidates the character memory cache. Metadata saves stay in the
chat save queue, do not cancel a pending full save, and recover an
integrity conflict with a forced full save inside the same queue task.

fix(chat): replace chat contents without spreading messages into arguments

Loading a chat replaced `chat[]` with `chat.splice(0, chat.length, ...data)`.

limit: V8 throws RangeError between 65,536 and 131,072 elements, so the
Android WebView could not open a chat of that size. JavaScriptCore has
no such limit, so desktop and iOS were unaffected.

`replaceChatContents()` writes the messages into the existing array and
adjusts its length, keeping the canonical `chat[]` instance stable. The
character, group, neutral-chat restore and import, and safety reset paths
all use it.
